title: Which shade are you? (Baguette Huggies, four shades)
format: reel (12 s, 1080x1920, 30 fps, seamless loop, designed cover; no audio track: add an instrumental from Instagram's Sound Collection at publish, ~100 bpm, downbeats on 3.0 / 4.8 / 6.6 / 8.4 s)
caption:
Which shade are you? Ruby, green, crystal or amethyst.

The Baguette Huggies: one row of crosswise cubic zirconia baguettes along a gold-tone huggie, in four shades. ₹1,199 a pair.

Tell us yours in the comments and we'll tell you what to wear them with.

[ baguette huggies · 18k gold tone plated · four shades, one pair ]

alt_text: Reel cover on pale sage: the words Which shade are you? above four tall fabric swatches with zigzag edges in ruby red, green, ivory and purple, each holding a pair of gold-tone huggie earrings set with a row of baguette stones in the matching colour, labelled ruby, green, crystal and amethyst, with the line Baguette Huggies, ₹1,199 a pair.

Reel: the camera moves into the ruby swatch and cuts to red silk filling the screen, named Ruby, for red, maroon and gold, with a small line under it: cubic zirconia; the silk lifts like a blind to a band at the top and shows a photograph of the ruby pair on a plaster block. On each beat it cuts to green silk and the green pair (for mehendi, bottle and parrot green; cubic zirconia, not emerald), ivory organza and the crystal pair (for ivory, pastels and silver; cubic zirconia), purple silk and the amethyst pair (for lilac, wine and purple; cubic zirconia). It ends on all four pairs in a row on pale sage: Four shades. One pair. Tell us yours. Baguette Huggies, ₹1,199 a pair, cubic zirconia, 18K gold tone plated, nairaflore.com. Then the words fade and the four pairs move back onto their swatches as the cover returns.

products.variant: Emerald (shown as GREEN: green cubic zirconia)

deviations: PHOTO RESOLUTION (slides 2-5). The spec scaled the 1200x1491 product photos 1.288x to 1546x1920 and pushed to 1.03 (1.33x past native). They show at most 1:1: 1200 wide, bottom-anchored (top y429, source x81-1161), push 0.97 to 1.00 about the bottom centre, so the hoops are crisp at ~630 px across. A 1:1 photo cannot reach the top of the frame, so each scene's words sit on a full-width band of that shade's silk (AI-1 texture, sheen, grain) with a pinked bottom edge at y600 and the swatch shadow. Type stays at the spec positions (Velista 88 b420, Cormorant 44 b484).

SILK-TO-PHOTO REVEAL (AD fix 2). The spec's 0.25 s opacity dissolve (silk to photo) is now a 0.40 s wipe on the full-frame silk's clip-path, INOUT, t0+0.30 to t0+0.70 (ruby 1.60-2.00): the pinked edge rises like a lifted blind from below the frame to y600 and stays there as the band. The dissolve washed the photo green or lilac and ghosted the hoops mid-way (3.4-3.5 s, 7.0-7.1 s); the wipe reveals the photo crisp with no colour wash. Two craft calls inside the fix: (a) the full-frame polygon is NF.pinked(1080,1928,16,8,'b'), not 1920: at 1920 the teeth's valleys sat at y1912 and showed slivers of the photo along the bottom of the full-bleed silk; the tooth count depends only on the width, so both polygons have 139 points and interpolate; (b) the separate band element is gone: the lifted silk IS the band (one element, so the band area cannot change through the reveal), and its wrapper carries the swatch shadow, so the rising edge casts a soft shadow onto the photo instead of moving as a flat cut.

RUBY ENTRY (replacing the spec's 1.50-1.80 cross-dissolve; retimed in the second AD pass). The cover holds 0-0.80 s (scale 1.00 to 1.02, linear), its eyebrow, headline and footer fade out 0.80-1.10, and the strip moves translate(0,0) scale(1) to translate(358px,-180px) scale(2) about (182,1140), INOUT 0.80-1.30, so the camera travels into ruby (its centre lands at 540,960 at 2.0x, the silk tile's native scale). It cuts hard to full-frame ruby silk at 1.30 s. The spec's dissolve muddied the sage to mauve, greyed the green swatch and turned the gold cut-outs copper. The cut was at 1.70 until this pass, which left ruby, the lead shade and the best seller, the weakest beat: RUBY. at 90% opacity or more for ~1.03 s, its turn ~0.93 s, the photo fully up ~0.70 s. Moving the cut to 1.30 gives ruby the same rule as the other three (silk lift t0+0.30 to t0+0.70, words at t0+0.08). The four downbeats (3.0 / 4.8 / 6.6 / 8.4) do not move, and frame 0 and cover.jpg are unchanged. If the owner wants the cover held longer, the alternative is to shift the four downbeats +0.3 s (3.3 / 5.1 / 6.9 / 8.7) and shorten the end card by 0.3 s.

WORDS ON THE DOWNBEAT. The shade name and turn go up at t0+0.08 s (1.38 / 3.08 / 4.88 / 6.68), on the full-frame silk, instead of after the reveal (spec: 1.80 / 3.60 / 5.40 / 7.20). The silk under the words is the same element through the lift, so they never jump. Measured on reel.mp4 (ink in the text box, linear in opacity): shade names at 90% or more for 1.43 s (ruby) and 1.50-1.53 s (the others); turn lines 1.30 s (ruby) and 1.40 s (the others). Every word holds past the 1.2 s rule.

SHEEN ACROSS THE STRIP (AD fix 4, adjusted). The cover's four swatches carried the identical 120 deg sheen (low-frequency light profiles correlated 0.99-1.00; the same pale blotch at y~1000-1150 on each). Added the optional o.sheenShift to NF.swatchSVG exactly as asked (gradient x1/x2 offset by -shift) with data-sheen-shift 0/239/478/717. Rendered literally, it lit ruby and one corner of green and left crystal and amethyst with no sheen at all: measured on a single 220x760 swatch, the 120 deg band is ~200 px wide and its isolines climb 1.7 px per px to the right, so one light cannot reach four swatches, and it cannot be 'high on ruby, low on amethyst' at 120 deg (it can only be low on the left and high on the right). Smallest sound change: the same shifts plus an optional o.sheenBox (data-sheen-box='937,760', the row's box), so the gradient line is measured on the whole strip. One window light now runs from ruby's lower right through green's middle to crystal's top and the corner of amethyst; profile correlations are now -0.07 to 0.80. Both options are optional; without them system.js returns byte-identical markup (checked on five swatch types), so no other post changes. Documented in _system/README.md 4.4.

COVER TYPE POSITIONS (AD fix 5). Eyebrow b350 (spec b330) and footer b1588 (spec b1610), so the 4:5 crop (y285-1635) keeps both inside its 45 px bands: eyebrow cap top at 50 px, footer baseline 47 px from the bottom. The eyebrow's baseline is 47 px above the headline's cap tops (y397); the footer's cap tops (y1572) clear the swatches' lowest teeth by ~40 px.

END-CARD PITCH (AD fix 6; grid-director fix, 26 Oct). Cut-out and label centres at x190 / 421 / 652 / 883, an equal 231 px pitch (was 233; spec 190 / 420 / 660 / 890). The pairs are 15% larger (230 wide, was 200), and at 233 the amethyst hoop's right edge would cross x1008 at the deepest drift; at 231 its hull ends at x993.5 (x1006.4 drifted). The hulls stand 10 px apart.

COVER CUT-OUTS 204 px wide (grid-director fix, 26 Oct; were 184), centred at swatch-local (110,150) (was (110,106.61), top edge at y800 on the pinked top edge, where the pairs read as specks at grid size). The pair's hull spans swatch-local x12-208 of the 220 px swatch, 4 px inside the teeth's valleys. Each cut-out and label rotates with its swatch (the spec did not say).

TURN COLOUR ON GREEN AND AMETHYST. The italic line is cream #F6EFE6, not the dark-ground blush-mid: on the sheened silk blush-mid measured about 4.3:1. Ruby keeps blush-mid; organza uses ink / ink-soft.

ORGANZA (cover swatch and crystal cut) carries the AI-1 silk texture as well as the sheen. That is the system default for light fills, and ai_elements lists the P7 colour cuts. Slide 4 said 'with sheen' only.

LOOP (second AD pass, fix 3). The end card's type fades out 11.40-11.62 s and the cover fades in 11.58-12.00 s (two staggered fades, not one 0.6 s cross-fade: overlapping both headline blocks ghosted FOUR SHADES under WHICH SHADE). The four end-card huggies no longer fade with it: they ride on a top layer and, INOUT 11.40-11.95, each travels from its end-card spot to its cover position (translate up to 16 px across and 60 px up, scale 0.887 = 230 to 204 px (since the 26 Oct pass), its swatch's rotation -1.5 / +1 / -1 / +1.5 deg) while the swatches, eyebrow, headline and footer fade in beneath. At 11.95 they hand off to the cover's own cut-outs, which are hidden 11.0-11.95. The pieces visibly go back onto their swatches; the near-empty sage frame at ~11.55 is gone. The hand-off changes the hoop boxes by 2.0-3.5/255 between frames 358 and 359, less than the frame before it (4.1-4.7, the swatches still fading in), and viewed at 2x it does not show. Frame 359 matches frame 0 at 1.15/255.

CAPTION (AD fix 7, and a claims fix). Paragraph 2 is now 'The Baguette Huggies: one row of crosswise cubic zirconia baguettes along a gold-tone huggie, in four shades. ₹1,199 a pair.' The spec's 'come in four, one row of ...' read as if 'four' were the row. 'cubic zirconia' stays in, so Ruby and Amethyst cannot read as gemstones (the post's claims_check). Paragraph 3 says 'what to wear them with' (a pair). COVER ALT TEXT says 'a pair of gold-tone huggie earrings': each swatch holds the pair.

KEYFRAME PRECISION. Keyframe percentages are written to 6 decimals: the ruby cut at 1.30 s is 10.833333% of 12 s, and 4 decimals put a cut microseconds after its frame, leaving a sliver of the cover on the first ruby frame.

END-CARD DRIFT (second AD pass, fix 2). The end card held perfectly still from 9.87 to 11.40 s (38 identical frames), which reads as a stall in a reel. Its type now sits in #end-drift (inside #end-content, which keeps the opacity fade), scaling linearly 1.000 at 8.40 s to 1.015 at 11.62 s, matching the cover's 1.00 to 1.02 drift; the huggies carry the same drift in their own transforms up to 11.40, so the card moves as one. One change from the brief: the origin is (72, 990) (26 Oct: (72, 840) before the card moved down 150 px), not (540, 990). Scaled about x540, every left-aligned line at x72 drifts out to x65, past the reel's x72 safe line. About x72 the left edge stays put and the far right reaches x1005 (the amethyst hoop, measured on frame 340, 11.33 s) at the deepest drift; every word stays inside x72-1008. At 1.5% over 3.2 s the direction does not read; it breathes. Every frame now moves (minimum step 0.19/255, was 0.000), and edge sharpness of the labels, price, plating and URL at 10.5 s is within 3% of the undrifted render.

END CARD MOVED DOWN (grid-director fix, 26 Oct). The block sat at about y400-1250 with ~650 px of empty sage below; headline, turn, four pairs, labels, price, kicker and URL move down 150 px (FOUR SHADES. b670, turn b750, pairs centred y970, labels b1150, price b1270, plating b1320, NAIRAFLORE.COM b1390) and the pairs scale 200 -> 230. Measured on frame 340: ink y596-1394, centred near y995 inside the y250-1650 band; x73-1005.

FULL-FRAME SILKS (grid-director fix 4, 26 Oct). The four full-frame silks are 1080 wide, so the system draws two broad soft sheen bands (15/35/55% at 0/.07/0 and 60/78/95% at 0/.05/0) instead of the one 120deg band, which showed on ruby and green as a hard diagonal glare stripe. The cover's 220 px swatches keep the single band (400 px or under).

Nothing else in the reel changed; alt text and caption unchanged (the footer copy is the same). In the 4:5 crop the footer baseline is 43px from the bottom (was 47).

Reel beats (grid-director fix, 26 Oct, in _work/build.py): each turn is now the match, the Matching Centre's job, instead of the same caveat four times in 7 s: RUBY 'for red, maroon and gold.' · GREEN 'for mehendi, bottle and parrot green.' · CRYSTAL 'for ivory, pastels and silver.' · AMETHYST 'for lilac, wine and purple.' (44px, b484, x72, the beat's turn colour, unchanged). The disclosure stays on screen on every beat as an a-kicker at b548 in the turn's colour, rising with the turn (class t2): '[ CUBIC ZIRCONIA ]' on ruby, crystal and amethyst, '[ CUBIC ZIRCONIA, NOT EMERALD ]' on green; inside the silk band (pinked edge ~y592-600). End card kicker '[ CUBIC ZIRCONIA · 18K GOLD TONE PLATED ]' (was '[ 18K GOLD TONE PLATED ]'), the reel's one plating line. The cover is unchanged (cover.html regenerated byte-identical).

No em dashes, exclamation marks, emoji, urgency or dates on the art or in the caption. No non-Latin strings in this post.
